title: Microcarrier-based spheroid 3D invasion assay for cell movement in ECM
author: Liu, Lu, et al.
materials: Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium (DMEM, D0819, Sigma)
Dulbecco’s Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS, Ca2+and Mg2+ free, D8537, Sigma-Aldrich)
Collagen type I, rat tail (08–115; Millipore)

Cytodex Microcarrier beads (C3275, Sigma-Aldrich) were hydrated in PBS for at least 3 h at room temperature. After beads settlement, discard the supernatant and add fresh Ca2+ and Mg2+ free PBS to a stock concentration of 50 ml/g. The beads in PBS are sterilized by autoclaving at 120 °C for 20 min and can be stored at 4 °C. Upon use, mix bead suspension in stock thoroughly and pipette 1 ml to a 15 ml Falcon tube. Centrifuge the mixture at 400 g for 5 min and aspirate the supernatant carefully. Re-suspend beads in a volume of 10 ml culture medium to make the final suspension.

steps.title: Prepare microcarrier beads
steps.instruction: Hydrate Cytodex Microcarrier beads (C3275, Sigma‑Aldrich) in PBS for ≥3 h at room temperature; discard supernatant, add Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑free PBS to a stock of 50 ml per gram of beads; autoclave the bead suspension at 120 °C for 20 min, then store at 4 °C. Before use, vortex the stock, pipette 1 ml into a 15 ml Falcon tube, centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min, carefully aspirate supernatant, and resuspend the beads in 10 ml culture medium to obtain the final bead suspension.

steps.title: Maintain cell cultures
steps.instruction: Grow human melanoma (BLM, M14, Mel57), colorectal cancer (SW480, CACO2) and mouse Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) cells in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle’s Medium supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum, at 5 % CO₂ and 37 °C.

steps.title: Form cell‑bead spheroids
steps.instruction: Suspend cells at 2–5 × 10⁵ cells ml⁻¹ in culture medium. Mix 1 ml cell suspension with 1 ml bead suspension in a round‑bottom snap‑cap tube (352,059, Corning). Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 6 h, manually shaking the tube gently every 2 h (continuous shaking on a shaker is not suitable). After 6 h, transfer the 2 ml mixture to a 6‑well plate or a 35 mm petri dish and incubate 1–2 days until most beads are fully covered with cells. Gently clap the plate to detach spheroids for downstream use. (Cell number required for confluence must be pre‑tested for each line.)

steps.title: Measure maximum migration distance
steps.instruction: Open the image file for the desired time point in AxioVision, select the “Circle” tool, draw a circle matching the bead (red circle) to obtain the bead radius, then draw a second circle from the same centre that encloses all migrating cells (white circle). Compute: Max migration distance (µm) = radius of migrating‑front circle – radius of bead circle.

steps.title: Calculate average max migration distance
steps.instruction: Open the image file for the desired time point in AxioVision, use the “Circle” tool to draw the bead circle and obtain its radius. Then select the “Curve” tool and trace a curve along the migrating front to generate a convex polygon; measure its perimeter. Compute: Avg. max migration distance (µm) = (perimeter of convex polygon ÷ 2π) – bead radius. (Only convex polygons give correct results.)

steps.title: Compute migration index
steps.instruction: In Fiji, open the z‑stack at the chosen time point, locate the bead and draw Circle0 that matches the largest bead diameter (record the macro). Create a z‑projection, set a threshold to include all cells, and replay the macro to recreate Circle0; measure its area (Area0). Draw successive concentric circles (Circle1, Circle2, …) each with a radius 10 µm larger than the previous one, measuring the area of each. For each circle i, calculate Area(i) = area of Circle(i) – area of Circle(i‑1). Export all areas to Excel, plot distance (i × 10 µm) versus Area(i) to visualise cell distribution, and compute the migration index using: Migration index = Σ_{i=1}^{n} 10 × i × Area(i). (Assuming uniform cell size, area is proportional to cell number.)

steps.title: Track cell trajectories and velocity
steps.instruction: Open the time‑lapse sequence for the selected position in Fiji, generate a z‑projection and adjust brightness/contrast for clear cell visibility. Use the “Manual tracking” plug‑in to follow individual cells across frames; the plugin outputs distance and velocity between successive slices. Export the results to Excel and calculate overall migration distance and velocity. (Alternative automated tracking tools may also be used.)
